uncited: This method connects 1D visualization views (such as Dynamic Volume Lines) with 3D volume rendering by using Hilbert space-filling curve codes to define selection ranges.
When a user selects a Region of Interest (ROI) in the 1D plot, the corresponding cells in the 3D view are highlighted.
- A set of ROIs defined in the 1D view, each specified by a start and end Hilbert code ($H_{start}, H_{end}$).
- A transfer function $T$ mapping scalar values to color and opacity.
- Highlighted cells in the 3D view corresponding to the selected ROIs.
**User Selection:** The user selects one or more ROIs in the 1D view.
**Ray Casting:** For each pixel, a ray is cast through the volume.
- **Hilbert Order:** Determined by the resolution of the volume grid.
- **AMR Data:** The Hilbert code of the cell centroid is insufficient to determine if a sample falls inside an ROI because cell sizes vary.
The GPU-accelerated implementation of Dynamic Volume Lines that uses this brushing and linking technique.
The process of mapping 3D voxel coordinates to 1D Hilbert codes.
This is a prerequisite for the selection method.
- **Time Complexity:** The containment test is $O(1)$ per sample per ROI range.
The overall complexity is dominated by the ray casting steps.
This method was introduced in the context of visual analysis of large multi-field AMR data on GPUs using Interactive Volume Lines.
